lines.en: We followed Lee Jihye straight into Chungmuro. Looking at the platform with its shattered screen doors, Yoo Sangah said,
“···There's something ominous about this place.”
As we made our way up along the Line 3 tracks, we spotted people sitting around and talking quietly.
[You have entered Chungmuro.]
[The third scenario is currently in progress.]
[Channel #GIR-8761 is active.]
[Channel #BIR-3642 is active.]
Starting at Chungmuro, the scenarios grew larger in scale, and the number of dokkaebi channels increased accordingly.
That guy Bihyung would have his work cut out for him from now on, too.
Just then, several middle-aged men spotted us and approached, waving.
“Oh, little samurai. Brought some newcomers?”
“Yeah.”
Samurai? They could only spout that crap because they didn't know who Lee Jihye's sponsor was. Those bastards would face divine punishment soon enough. Lee Jihye scowled at the middle-aged men.
“Been guzzling booze again?”
“Hahaha! With the world in this state, what else is there to do but drink?”

The middle-aged men, with their comfortably rounded builds like neighborhood real estate agents, seemed far too relaxed for people caught in a disaster. Each also carried a weapon as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
This was certainly different from Geumho Station.
I supposed the people we'd be dealing with from here on were the real deal.
“So, did you folks fight your way through the Dongguk University tunnel? Impressive··· Must've made yourselves a few coins?”
That was when one of the middle-aged men turned his gaze toward Yoo Sangah.
“What's your name, young lady? I've got a cheap room. Want to rent it?”
“···A room?”
“Haha, you don't know how things work here yet, do you, young lady? You see, here—”
Lee Jihye cut the man off.
“Ajusshis. Stop trying your bullshit on the newcomers and get back upstairs.”
“Now, now, they'll need to know anyway. We're all just trying to survive······.”
“If you don't want to fucking die.”
The middle-aged men went pale at Lee Jihye's words as she drew her gleaming blue longsword.
“You······ So young, and already you've learned nothing but bad manners.”
“Hey, Kang-ssi. Leave it. Let's go.”
The middle-aged men walked away, looking back at us with lingering regret. Only after they disappeared into the transfer passage for Line 4 did Lee Jihye sheathe her sword.
“I've brought you here, so you're on your own now. I'm not playing babysitter.”
What a mouth on this kid.
I took a moment to look around.
Chungmuro.
This place, the setting of the third scenario, was governed by rules entirely different from those we'd encountered so far.
“F-Fuck! Come any closer and I'll kill you all······.”
In the middle of the Line 3 platform, a man holding a knife glared threateningly at everyone around him.
Beneath his feet was a tiled area that looked a little larger than one pyeong, with green light hovering over it. Yoo Sangah asked,
“···Why is he acting like that?”
“I don't know either.”
I actually had an idea, but there was no need to tell her right now and scare her.
People who looked much like the man with the knife sat slumped all around the Line 3 platform.
Unlike the middle-aged men from earlier, every one of their faces was steeped in despair. Glancing over them, I asked Lee Jihye,
“Yoo Joonghyuk's here, right?”
At the name ‘Yoo Joonghyuk,’ Lee Jihye, who had been about to leave, whipped her head around. Her eyes were wary.
“···Who the hell are you?”
Judging by the way she spoke, Yoo Joonghyuk had already ruined the kid.

I could understand it. Even if you searched all of Korea, a constellation on the level of the Maritime War God would be hard to find. If I'd been in Yoo Joonghyuk's position, I would've sought this kid out as soon as I reached Chungmuro, too.
“I'm Yoo Joonghyuk's companion who made it back alive.”
“···Companion? That can't be right, can it?”
Lee Jihye, staring at me with deep suspicion. I shrugged shamelessly.
“Tell him that, and he'll understand. Where's Yoo Joonghyuk now?”
“···Master isn't here right now.”
“Really? That's a problem. There's something I have to tell him.”
Her expression twisting, Lee Jihye glared at me for a moment, then looked somehow utterly betrayed.
Well, I could see exactly what this kid thought of Yoo Joonghyuk. And she was already calling him ‘Master’······ Losing the general to him like this would be a problem.
Lee Jihye called out to a boy curled up in a corner, trying to sleep.
“Hey, you!”
“Huh? Yes, yes!”
“Keep an eye on these people! I'm going to see Master, then I'll be back.”
The boy looked at us in bewilderment.
“······Who are they?”
“Don't know. Says he's Master's friend!”
At Lee Jihye's words, the people sprawled around the platform opened their eyes one by one. They looked at us, half with curiosity and half with awe.
“······Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi's friend?”
The boy hurried over and peered at us. He looked roughly the same age as Lee Jihye.
“Are you really a friend of Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi?”
Wide, bright eyes. Looking into the boy's innocent eyes, it was simply impossible to lie. For an ordinary person, that is.
“We're very close friends.”
Lately, I'd been thinking that perhaps I wasn't an ‘ordinary person’ after all.
At least not here.
While Yoo Sangah tended to the unconscious Jung Heewon, I heard about Chungmuro from the boy.
He was one of the few who followed Yoo Joonghyuk, along with Lee Jihye.
“······And that's why we follow Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi. Um, are you listening?”
“Yes.”
Of course, I wasn't really listening.
Heroic tales about that psychopath Yoo Joonghyuk weren't remotely interesting.
Still, to sum it up, it went something like this.
“Yoo Joonghyuk showed up here three days ago and saved Lee Jihye and a few of you from a horde of monsters. That's basically it, isn't it?”
With his personal account so brutally condensed, the boy looked completely dumbfounded.
“Uh, can you really make it sound that simple······?”
He seemed thoroughly bewitched by Yoo Joonghyuk.
Well, when someone with overwhelming martial power suddenly appeared and saved them, it would've been stranger if they didn't follow him.
But the boy probably didn't know.
That he had survived because he'd been lucky enough to be with Lee Jihye, rather than because Yoo Joonghyuk was a good person.
“Excuse me, there are a few things I'd like to know. May I ask?”
While I was lost in thought, Lee Hyunsung politely began asking questions.
“Yes. Go ahead.”
“How do you obtain food supplies here?”
“Well, calling it a supply system is a bit embarrassing······ A few of us, myself included, mostly depend on Jihye. Jihye hunts and asks Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi to cook what she catches······.”
When had he made another checklist? Lee Hyunsung rummaged around, pulled out a notebook, and began writing something down. A soldier through and through.
“Then what do you do for drinking water?”
“We get a little at a time from the ‘Landlord Alliance’ upstairs in exchange for food or coins.”
“···Landlord Alliance?”
I shifted in my seat.
It looked like things were finally getting interesting. The boy hesitated a little before speaking.
“There are some landlords who used to run the Chungmuro area. They've taken over the upper floors. We call them the Landlord Alliance.”
The Chungmuro Landlord Alliance.
A name that appeared in ‘Ways of Survival,’ too.
“What sort of people are they?”
“Well, I'm not sure how to put it······.”
It was a question I didn't actually need to ask.
If my expectations were right, the person currently ruling Chungmuro was probably one of the ‘10 Evils (十惡).’
“They're just landlords.”
The answer he gave with a sigh was, in a sense, correct. They were landlords. Landlords who merely collected the set rent.
That was when Lee Gilyoung, who had been quiet, spoke up.
“Um, hyung.”
“Yeah?”
“I need to use the bathroom.”
“Is it urgent?”
“Yes.”

The timing was a little unexpected. It was all the more puzzling because Lee Gilyoung had never spoken to me about anything like this before. But Yoo Sangah was standing right beside him, her face flushed.
“···Um, could I go with him, too?”

For a moment, I remembered Yoo Sangah and Jung Heewon gathering some secret necessities at Yaksu Station. I thought I understood what was going on. That little rascal Lee Gilyoung was sharp for his age.
The boy, who'd overheard the conversation, said,
“You'll have to go up to the second basement level for the bathrooms, but getting in won't be easy.”
“···Is something wrong?”
“Hmm. I think it'd be better to see for yourselves··· I was just about to head up, too. Would you like to come along?”
“Let's have a look.”
I was the one who said that.
Of course, I wasn't actually going to use the bathroom. There were a few things I needed to check upstairs.
Yoo Joonghyuk's recent actions were unfolding in ways subtly different from the ‘third round’ I knew. That meant I needed to establish exactly what those differences were.
With Jung Heewon still unconscious on my back, I went up to the third basement level with the others.
“Oh, the new faces from earlier. Come to look at a ‘room’?”
The middle-aged men standing near the Line 4 escalator whistled and asked. The boy shook his head as he answered.
“Ah, sorry. We just have something to do upstairs······.”
“Aw, that's a shame. Take care, then.”
The middle-aged man waved us on without further fuss. Watching him move away, Yoo Sangah tilted her head and asked,
“Um, by the way······ Everyone keeps using the word ‘room.’ What exactly do they mean? It doesn't seem to be the kind of room I'm thinking of.”
“Put simply, that's one.”
Where the boy pointed, tiles formed a square on the floor.
They were the same kind of tiles we'd seen on the Line 3 platform earlier. Again, green tiles covering what looked like a little more than one pyeong.
Looking closely, I could see something written in the air above the tiles.
[Green Zone 0/1]
“The scenario calls them ‘Green Zones,’ but here we call them ‘rooms.’”
Right beside the tiles, two men were grappling with each other.
As though they were fighting over those tiles. This time, Lee Hyunsung asked,
“What exactly is that? Why are those people fighting over it?”
The boy looked a little reluctant. As if telling us would somehow threaten his own survival.
“You'll find out everything when we reach the second basement level.”
The higher we went, the more often we saw fights over ‘rooms.’
The numbers attached to each room varied, from (0/1) for the small ones to (0/7) for the large ones.
The second number probably indicated how many people it could accommodate.
Carefully surveying our surroundings, I asked,
“Does everything from the third basement level to the first belong to the ‘Landlord Alliance’?”
“······Yes. There are a few smaller factions, too, but the Landlord Alliance has pretty much taken it all.”
All of Chungmuro's amenities were concentrated on the first and second basement levels, so in effect, a single alliance held a monopoly on all the power.
“Isn't Yoo Joonghyuk doing anything about it? You said he saved you.”
The boy's face visibly darkened at my question. His lips moved for a long time before he finally managed to get the words out.
“He just told us to stand on our own······.”
That figured. The Yoo Joonghyuk I knew would've said exactly that sort of crap. He probably hadn't ever told them to follow him.
Captivated by the overwhelming martial power Yoo Joonghyuk had displayed, these people were nursing a slender hope all on their own.
Poor things.
Before long, we arrived at the second basement level. Tension crept over the boy's face.
“You'll need to be careful from here on.”
The second basement level had far more ‘rooms’ than the floors below.
But few people were touting for customers as before. Instead, we saw only people guarding their Green Zones with fierce eyes.
[Green Zone 7/7]
We walked straight past them toward the bathrooms.
“Uh······ Why has everyone stopped here?”
We came to a halt just before the final passage to the bathrooms. Dozens of people were gathered at a nearby bottleneck.
“Let's go to the front.”
With that, I pushed through the crowd.
“Pildu-ssi! Please take us back! We won't do it again!”
“Please, please! Let us stay just one more day. I'll get the coins, even if I have to borrow them!”
The front of the crowd seethed with people's desperate fervor.
“Now, now, step back. Step back.”
Facing them, people who appeared to belong to the ‘Landlord Alliance’ stood in a row, holding weapons. I knew instinctively.
One of the ‘10 Evils’ must be here.
I tried to identify that member of the ‘10 Evils’ from the novel's description, but they all looked so similar that picking him out wasn't easy.
Did becoming a landlord make everyone look alike?
That was when something wriggled near my legs and poked its head out.
It was Lee Gilyoung. It looked dangerous, so I reached for his shoulder, but just then, someone shoved him.
“Ah!”
Lee Gilyoung lost his balance and fell, catching himself with a hand on the floor.
[The individual ‘Lee Gilyoung’ has trespassed on private property!]
The atmosphere turned icy in an instant, and several members of the ‘Landlord Alliance’ in the front row looked at Lee Gilyoung.
“Who are you, brat?”
Almost at the same time, the gathered crowd screamed and backed away.
“Shit!”
“G-Get back! Hurry!”
As though they'd seen something they shouldn't, the tightly packed crowd receded like an ebbing tide.
Once the people were gone, a boundary line glowing red became visible where they'd stood.
A man looked between the boundary and Lee Gilyoung as he spoke.
“Hmm. Looks like you're lost. Do you know where you are?”
“Isn't this the way to the bathrooms?”
“The bathrooms? Haha, it used to be. But you little bastard······ Where are your parents?”
“Were you taught not to wander onto someone else's land, or weren't you?”
‘Someone else's land,’ huh.
Well, that settled it.
With an unreadable look in his eyes, the man stroked Lee Gilyoung's head and said,
“Little brat, looks like you don't know. Then let me teach you.”
[The stigma 「Armed Zone Lv.3」 of the character ‘Gong Pildu’ activates!]
A high-pitched mechanical whine sounded, and miniature turrets resembling Gatling guns rose from the floor all around us at once.
[The character ‘Gong Pildu’ demands payment of 500 coins for trespassing on private property.]
[Failure to comply will cause all nearby turrets to open fire immediately.]
The man said,
“Hand over the money, brat.”
Having finished loading their ammunition, all the turrets were aimed at Lee Gilyoung.
Flustered, Lee Gilyoung backed away in hesitant steps and pressed against my side. The man smiled when he noticed me.
“Ah, so you have a guardian. Then your guardian should pay the 500 coins for you, shouldn't he?”
Looking at the hand the man abruptly held out, I smiled.
······Interesting, Yoo Joonghyuk.
So you've left bastards like these alone?
The 10 Evils (十惡).

Though the roster and rankings sometimes changed depending on which round of life Yoo Joonghyuk was in, they were the ten people who served as the principal villains in the world of ‘Ways of Survival.’
Gong Pildu, Chungmuro's Armed Fortress Master (武裝城主), was one of those 10 Evils.
Anyone who'd read Ways of Survival to the end (only me, admittedly) couldn't possibly be unfamiliar with Gong Pildu.
[Green Zone 56/70]
Sure enough, even the size of his ‘room’ was on another level. A room whose area was difficult to estimate in pyeong.
This whole area was Gong Pildu's ‘Green Zone.’
Should I try the standard approach first?
Moving Lee Gilyoung behind me, I spoke.
“Why are you charging coins? Chungmuro Station is a public facility.”
“Haha, it was until eight days ago. But not anymore.”
For an ordinary person, 500 coins was by no means a small sum.
Yet they wanted 500 coins just for stepping onto their land······ They were nothing but thieves.
“Fine, I'll pay. But I'll hand it over directly.”
“What?”
“You're not Gong Pildu, are you?”
He'd been running his mouth as if he were Gong Pildu himself, but the man before me was merely Extra 1 of the ‘Landlord Alliance.’
Where are you, Gong Pildu?
I quickly scanned the surroundings. Not that one, or that one······ If I were Gong Pildu, where would I be?
“Haha, you're a funny bastard. Hey, are you messing with me right now······.”
“Gong Pildu-ssi. Where are you? Come collect your fine.”
I ignored the man and walked on.
[You have trespassed on private property!]
A turret rose and immediately aimed at me, but I didn't stop.
Honestly, if those turrets opened fire, there was no guarantee even I would get out unscathed. But I needed to show some nerve here. Otherwise, Gong Pildu would look down on me.
“That's far enough. Come any closer and I'll kill you.”
And at last, Gong Pildu made his move.
A bench piled with all sorts of everyday necessities. The middle-aged man who had been sitting on it reading a magazine was looking my way.
Sure enough, he was exactly as the novel had described.
A slightly protruding belly and a half-bald head. This was Gong Pildu, the leader of the ‘Landlord Alliance.’
“Haven't seen your face before. You've got quite some nerve.”
“Having to come here and pay is bad enough. Do I need to tiptoe around you, too?”
[The character ‘Gong Pildu’ takes an interest in you.]
Anyway, I was popular with villains. Kim Namwoon had been the same.
“You've got quite a tongue on you. But you'd better not get too cocky.”
Click. I heard a turret load a magic bullet. Fucking bastard.
Gong Pildu, smiling like an ordinary guy from the neighborhood. But I knew. Gong Pildu was absolutely no ‘ordinary guy from the neighborhood.’

There were countless people in the world who held the ‘upper hand,’ but few held it as securely as landlords or great landowners. Yet someone possessed both those attributes: Gong Pildu before me, who would later be called the ‘Armed Fortress Master.’
Reading the explanation like this made it feel all the more real.
As if having two attributes weren't enough, his Magic Power was already level 19.
I supposed it took at least this much to secure even one of the places among the 10 Evils later on.
“So, what brings you here? It doesn't look like you're here just to hand over a fine.”
As expected, he was unusually perceptive.
For a brief moment, I considered my options.
Negotiate here, or subdue Gong Pildu right away.

I might have a chance if I went all out from the start, but Gong Pildu's ‘Armed Zone’ was by no means an easy stigma to deal with. If I tried to subdue him, I'd have to be prepared to take turret fire and suffer serious injuries myself.
What to do? I had other uses for my coins, so I couldn't put them into more stats, either.
“Just a word of caution: you'd better not be getting any funny ideas.”
Smiling, Gong Pildu looked behind me. The alliance's armed forces had already surrounded Lee Hyunsung and the others. Sure enough, that brain of his worked damn fast.
I smiled and raised both hands.
“Let's stay calm. Isn't it obvious why a tenant would come to a landlord?”
“A room?”
“Yes. Please allow my companions and me to stay in your Green Zone, Pildu-ssi.”
This was absolutely necessary.
To clear the third scenario safely, we had to stay in Gong Pildu's ‘Green Zone.’
But Gong Pildu's answer was just as expected.
“No. The alliance doesn't accept outsiders. I might consider it if each of you paid 500 coins every day.”
500 coins every day? He talked as if he were selling some product for coins. This bastard was worse than the Dokkaebi Bag.
“That would be difficult. I'll give you information instead.”
“What information?”
“Information about Yoo Joonghyuk.”
Yoo Joonghyuk. That name alone made the landlords' expressions change abruptly.
“Yoo Joonghyuk? You mean the one who went on that rampage a little while ago······.”
“You bastard! What's your connection to him?”
“Pildu-ssi! There's something suspicious about this guy!”
Sure enough, that got a reaction.
I'd figured Yoo Joonghyuk would already have had trouble with the ‘Landlord Alliance.’
Actually, that was what bothered me a little.

According to the original story, Yoo Joonghyuk in his third regression round should've been locked in a bloody battle with the ‘Landlord Alliance’ by now. Where was that bastard, and what was he doing?
Gong Pildu looked at me suspiciously and asked,
“What's your connection to Yoo Joonghyuk?”
“We're companions who've faced life and death separately.”
“···Not together?”
“Anyway, the point is that we're close.”
“How am I supposed to believe that?”
“Don't believe me, then. You have nothing to lose either way, do you?”
I tossed the words out casually.
Gong Pildu probably wouldn't be able to refuse my offer.
Because Yoo Joonghyuk was currently the only person in Chungmuro who threatened Gong Pildu's power.
[The character ‘Gong Pildu’ activates 「Profit Calculation Lv.2」.]
“What do you mean, nothing to lose?”
“There's no guarantee you're not a con artist. Don't underestimate experience. In my experience, guys who look just like you are always the ones who skip out without paying their rent.”
His remark felt so pointed and accurate that I even felt wronged. But I couldn't afford to lose this war of words.
“······If you don't believe me, there's nothing I can do. It's your loss anyway.”
Gong Pildu's expression grew conflicted at my words. I turned away without hesitation. It was important to show no reluctance to leave. That would make him all the more reluctant to let me go.
“Wait.”
Just as expected.
“You still have to pay the trespassing fine. Where do you think you're running off to?”
So he was reluctant for a different reason. Damn bastard. Smiling awkwardly, I turned back.
“How much was it? 100 coins?”
“No, 1000 coins for you and that kid combined.”
A vein bulged on my forehead.
Did this bastard think 1000 coins were just a single 1000-won bill······?
“That's too much.”
I'd never had that many coins extorted from me even by a dokkaebi. I couldn't give 1000 coins to a bastard like Gong Pildu.
Gong Pildu smiled.
“Then you're disqualified as a tenant. Die.”
Instinctively, I shoved aside the men around me and ran toward my companions. Boom—the first shot rang out, and Lee Hyunsung was already covering my back with his steel shield.
He really was dependable.
“······Dokja-ssi.”
But even Lee Hyunsung, whose Strength and Constitution were both approaching level 14, sounded extremely tense.
The trembling muscles in his arms made it clear.
With his second stigma yet to awaken, Lee Hyunsung's stats couldn't withstand sustained fire from those turrets.
And Jung Heewon was out of commission, too. If we fought them head-on here, someone in our group would certainly die.
“Gong Pildu-ssi, wait a moment.”
Then I couldn't get into a fight that would leave us worse off.
“What now?”
“You'd be better off not fighting us right now.”
“Why?”
Someone else would have to take the loss.
“Because if you fight now, you'll die here.”
Gong Pildu's expression hardened. Even without further explanation, he must have just noticed, too.
The presence of the man now descending the escalator that led to the first basement level.
With him radiating such a tremendous aura, it would've been strange not to notice.
“My very dear companion is on his way.”
Yoo Joonghyuk.
Who would've thought I'd be so glad to see that fucking regressor bastard?
“Master, that's him. That's the guy who falsely claimed to be your companion.”
Lee Jihye was pointing at me, her voice shrill. And striding along beside her was our protagonist, starring in a drama all by himself. The murderous glare he directed at me was very impressive.
[The character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ is greatly shaken.]
[Stage 2 of the exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’ activates!]
A brief wave of dizziness swept over me, and then I began to hear his thoughts.
「How······ Already?」
I waved at him with an innocent smile.
“Hi, Joonghyuk.”
“How've you been? You're looking good, aren't you?”

Lee Jihye and Gong Pildu looked back and forth between Yoo Joonghyuk and me in disbelief. As if there were absolutely no way Yoo Joonghyuk and I could be ‘companions.’ The air began to grow taut with tension.
“These people don't believe you and I are companions. Could you tell them for me?”
But I knew Yoo Joonghyuk.
This bastard killed people as routinely as he ate, but he always kept his promises.
[A small number of constellations pay attention to the answer from the character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ watches to see whether the character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ will keep his word.]
Especially when the constellations were watching, as they were now.
After regarding me with a quiet gaze, Yoo Joonghyuk slowly opened his mouth. But I spoke first.
“Oh, and it'd be even better if you could get them to let us use the bathrooms!”
At last, Yoo Joonghyuk drew his sword.
A little while later, having used the bathrooms without incident, we were back down on the Line 3 platform. All thanks to having such a good regressor companion. I smiled and said,
“Good to see you, bastard.”
“······So you were alive after all.”
To get straight to the point, Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't called me his companion. Instead, he had answered by quietly pointing his sword at Gong Pildu.
Fortunately, Gong Pildu hadn't wanted a clash and had let us go, though he ground his teeth.
“Were you hoping I'd died?”
“I thought it didn't matter either way.”
Companion, my ass.
Seeing that smug face again after so long only made me angrier. I wanted to run over and knock his jaw off right then and there, but I couldn't.

It hadn't made much of an impression when I read the novel, but seeing it in person made it clear just how extraordinary this bastard was.
We were only just entering the third scenario, yet his Constitution, Strength, and Agility already added up to more than 70. Wasn't this guy completely insane?
Damn it, these protagonist buffs.
“Do you have anything else to say?”
Still, for some reason, it bothered me that he was growing faster than in the original third round.
Growing faster meant he was taking correspondingly greater risks··· What kind of bullshit was a guy only in his third regression round plotting?
I was starting to feel uneasy. I'd have to investigate him discreetly soon······.
“I asked if you had anything to say.”
“No, I was just looking because you piss me off.”
「···He certainly has resolve.」
Resolve, my ass.
He was just drowning in his own chuunibyou.
「Still, that arrogance won't do. Should I just kill him now?」
“I'm joking.”
I said hastily, with a smile.
Yoo Joonghyuk turned his head away as if uninterested.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is disappointed in you.]
I hadn't intended to beat Yoo Joonghyuk up right now anyway.
Yoo Joonghyuk was indispensable to clearing the countless scenarios still ahead.
Even if we didn't act like real companions, he was worth exploiting down to his very bones.
······Why did that sound like a pathetic excuse when I was telling the truth?
“It seems you've gathered companions.”
With an expressionless gaze, Yoo Joonghyuk looked at me, then at the people behind me.
[The character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ is slightly disappointed in you.]
······What? Why?
I soon found out the answer.
[The character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ activates ‘Sage's Eye Lv.8’!]
「I went to the trouble of leaving Lee Hyunsung behind, and this is as far as he's managed to develop him?」
It was true, and for a moment I was at a loss for words. Certainly, Lee Hyunsung would've progressed further by now if he'd gone with Yoo Joonghyuk.
Still······ You bastard.
